summary: The change adds a Go runtime function abap.DecodeBase64 and a nodeutf8 package, but never wires CL_HTTP_UTILITY=>DECODE_BASE64 into the gogen frontend's kernel-call table, so ABAP calls are still NOT_COMPILED. The UTF-8 decoder also diverges from Node whenever a sequence with an invalid second byte (E0 80, ED A0, F0 8F, F4 90) is interrupted by a non-continuation byte mid-stream, emitting one U+FFFD where Node emits one per byte.

findings.claim: No mapping for CL_HTTP_UTILITY=>IF_HTTP_UTILITY~DECODE_BASE64 (next to ENCODE_BASE64's {fn: "abap.EncodeBase64", args: ["UNENCODED:string"]}) was added, so the new abap.DecodeBase64 is unreachable from compiled ABAP; the call still hits the @KERNEL line and reports NOT_COMPILED. The hidden acceptance test ZCL_OSGT_DECODE_BASE64 fails for this reason.
findings.repro: A class whose method does `rv = cl_http_utility=>decode_base64( iv ).` plus a unit test, then `node tools/osgo-unit.mjs /tmp/b64case --class ZCL_OSGT_DECODE_BASE64` -> `NOT_COMPILED in CL_HTTP_UTILITY=>IF_HTTP_UTILITY~DECODE_BASE64 (cl_http_utility.clas.abap:159): @KERNEL`

findings.claim: The decoder checks only the generic 80..BF continuation range for the second byte and does not check the lead byte's own range (E0:A0-BF, ED:80-9F, F0:90-BF, F4:80-8F). When an invalid prefix like E0 80 or F4 90 80 is then broken by a non-continuation byte, it emits a single U+FFFD for the whole prefix. Node (WHATWG maximal-subpart) emits one per byte. A differential fuzz over 200k short byte strings found 5328 mismatches with Node.
findings.repro: nodeutf8.Decode("\xE0\x80A") == "\uFFFDA" but Node Buffer.from('e08041','hex').toString() == "\uFFFD\uFFFDA"; likewise \xED\xA0A and \xF4\x90\x80A (Node: 3 U+FFFD + A, Go: 1)

findings.claim: Overlong, surrogate and out-of-range handling is split three ways (decodeSequence after completion, wouldBeValid at EOF, nothing mid-stream), which is how the mid-stream case was missed. Validating the second byte against the lead byte's range when it arrives would cover all three paths at once. The tests cover the EOF and complete-sequence cases only.
